correctness.rationale: Every one-point type corresponds bijectively to disjoint lower ideal and upper filter (L,U) with all L below all U, by finite-poset transitivity and the Fraïssé extension property. A singleton upper filter is exactly one rooted-tree leaf; allowed lower ideals are its unique ancestor-chain prefixes, giving [u^d v] E_T as the leaf depth tail at all sizes. The ideal polynomial obeys I_T=1+u product I_children. A complete canonical multiset-of-children enumeration checks all 85 rooted shapes through size seven, with unique first collision at seven; independent direct L,U enumeration confirms the mixed coefficient witnesses. No infinite claim follows from finite testing.

value.rationale: The ideal-rank polynomial is a classical natural object, and its sharp first loss of rooted-tree information at seven vertices is an exact inverse/identifiability boundary. The richer model-theoretic grading recovers leaf-depth tails for every rooted tree, distinguishing a uniquely minimal ambiguous pair. This addresses structural information retained and lost by natural type spectra rather than arbitrary numerical slices.
